# Pre-registered retrieval evaluation (round 1 vs round 2)

*Generated by `rag_eval.py` at 2026-11-10 01:19 UTC. Metric definitions and aliases live in `experiments/gold.json` (sha256 `ea2393a0091761ce03d1125a0d9a81e145f3f2bc6395f870f87c15afc4aacf07`), registered before any round-2 run.*

**Read before comparing rows:**

- **Embedding window.** The embedding model (`paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2`) reads only the first 128 tokens of each chunk; the rest of a longer chunk never reaches dense retrieval, while BM25 indexes the full chunk text. This is a possible confound when reading F: part of a difference between F and E′ may come from BM25 seeing text the embedding never read, not from lexical matching as such.
- **Loose alias.** The gold alias `Pete` (for Popin' Pete) is loose: any standalone "Pete" counts, so the Q2 member counts can include a different Pete.
- **What each round used.** Round-1 rows come from an index of 39 documents (`experiments/corpus_round1.json`) and from gemini-2.5-flash answers via a course proxy. Round-2 rows use the model and corpus recorded in their results.json; each round-2 row label names its corpus and run folder.

## Metrics

- **Mean cosine distance to question (5 Qs)**: for each fixed question, the mean cosine distance between the original question and each retrieved chunk, averaged over the five questions (round 1: distances recorded in `q1.md`–`q5.md`; round 2: `distance_to_question`). Context, not a quality score: with a fixed k the dense top-k is by construction the minimum-distance set, so hybrid fusion (F) or query expansion (G) can only keep or raise it.
- **Q2 members named (/9)**: how many of the nine notable Electric Boogaloos members listed in the corpus (Boogaloo Sam, Popin' Pete, Skeeter Rabbit, Suga Pop, Mr. Wiggles, Jazzy J, Creepin Cid, Puppet Boozer, Robot Dane) the Q2 answer names. Matching uses the gold aliases, case-insensitive, never inside a longer Latin-letter word.
- **Q2 members in context (/9)**: the same nine names found in the retrieved chunk texts (file names in the prompt's source headers are not counted).
- **Q4 Juste Debout chunks in top-k**: retrieved Q4 chunks that mention "Juste Debout" together with at least one fact group (format, city, year, venue, organizer), shown as hits/retrieved.
- **Q4 fact groups in answer**: fact groups (0–5) the Q4 answer states, counted only when the answer mentions Juste Debout.
- `n/a`: no answer to score (retrieval-only run or LLM error). When query expansion failed for a question, its retrieval metrics are n/a too and it is left out of the mean distance.
- Max distance: F applies it to the dense channel only (BM25-only chunks bypass it); G applies it to each sub-query's distance, not to the original question.

## Rounds

- **Round 1** (A–E, April 2026): rows reuse the answers and distances recorded in `experiments/combo_a`–`combo_e`; nothing was re-run. Model: gemini-2.5-flash (course OpenAI-compatible proxy). The round-1 index held 39 documents (`experiments/corpus_round1.json`; `data/processed` now holds 42). Chunk texts were not stored, so they are rebuilt by re-chunking `data/processed/<source_file>` with each combo's round-1 chunker, after checking that `data/processed` matches `experiments/corpus_pin.json` (digest `c8e76a3ac522…`, text committed before round 1); 115/115 rebuilt chunks reproduce the section label recorded next to their cite.
- **Round 2** (E′ control, F hybrid, G query expansion): read from 6 run folder(s) under `experiments/round2`. Model: gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14. Round-2 chunk texts and distances come from `results.json`, i.e. from the index built at run time.
- Within one run folder, rag_eval scores round 2 only when every combo shares the model, retrieval mode, embedding model, corpus (name, document count, document-list digest), chunk count, indexed-text hash and git commit; otherwise it refuses to score. Across run folders, rows are grouped by (corpus, model) and each label names the corpus and the run folder. Compare F and G with E′ from the same run folder. Round-1 E vs E′ mixes a model change with the re-index.
- `experiments/round2/round1_corpus/run1` (round1 corpus · run 1): model gpt-4.1-mini-2025-04-14, retrieval + answer, embedding paraphrase-multilingual-MiniLM-L12-v2, round1 corpus of 39 documents (list sha256 `ee060c510ca6…`), 1248 chunks, indexed text matches the pinned text of its 39 documents (data/processed, sha256 `5da23af5900e…`), git commit `c728f5a`.
